name: Heap object
first: Memory on the heap, found by its address.

dependsOn.why: A heap object stays after the call that made it returns, and a stack frame does not.

sil.shows: Score() makes its object on the heap.
score holds the object's address, and is not itself kept on the heap.

what.is: The heap is memory that does not belong to any one call, so it is not removed when a call returns. A heap object is one piece of the heap, made while the program runs, and found by its address.

caption.title: A `Score` object on the heap,
caption.text: while `makeScore()` runs, and after it returns.

what.afterExample: `Score()` on line 5 makes an instance of the class `Score`, and the instance is a heap object. `score` does not hold the object itself: it holds the object's address, which Swift calls a reference to the object.
what.problem: Some values must stay after the call that made them returns, and be used from more than one place. A stack frame cannot keep them, because it is removed when its call returns.
what.how: A heap object stays while something holds its address. When `makeScore()` returns, `score` is removed with its frame, but `mine` holds the same address, so the object stays.

memory.question: `score` is removed when `makeScore()` returns. What happens to the `Score` object?

steps.text: Line 8 calls `makeScore()`. A stack frame is made for the call. `score` has no value yet.
Line 5 makes a `Score` object on the heap, with `points` set to 0. `score`, in the frame, holds its address.
Line 6 returns `score`, and the frame is removed, so `score` no longer exists. Line 8 stores the returned address in `mine`. The object stays, because `mine` holds its address.

memory.answer: The object stays, because `mine` holds its address. A heap object stays while something holds its address.
